children: Novo Nordisk (NVO, Financials) is getting another data point for its oral Wegovy program, with real-world study suggesting that those who recently gained weight can get higher weight-loss effects from the medication.

The observational study involved more than 3,000 patients who had not previously used GLP-1 medications. Those who had gained weight in the past five years were more likely to be super-responders, meaning they lost at least 10 percent of their body weight.

By day 60, the super-responders had lost an average of 7.2% of their body weight, and by day 90, they had lost 11.4%. The group also had higher reductions in blood pressure than people who lost less weight.
The study indicated that super-responders also were more likely to have been prescribed larger dosages of oral Wegovy earlier in therapy.

Yet the findings had obvious limitations. It being an observational study, the follow-up period was short, and the researchers characterized the data as hypothesis-generating. This paper has not been peer reviewed yet.
The findings add to Novo Nordisk's body of knowledge on how patients may respond to oral semaglutide, as the company pushes into non-injectable weight-loss medicines.
The next trigger is future study to see whether the association between recent weight increase, dose, and a better treatment response maintains in broader patient populations.

title: Novo's Oral Wegovy Just Revealed a Surprising Weight-Loss Signal
